name: Seladelpar

lead: Seladelpar is a prescription PPAR-delta agonist approved in the US in 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis, a chronic liver disease. Fat-loss circles follow it because PPAR-delta is the same receptor targeted by GW501516-type compounds, which are promoted for endurance, greater fat burning and leanness.

It activates PPAR-delta, which reduces bile acid synthesis in liver cells; the label says the precise mechanism in PBC is not well understood. Its trials measure liver markers and itch, not fat loss or looks.

paras: Its documented use is a once-daily prescription for adults with PBC, taken with ursodeoxycholic acid or alone if that is not tolerated. Use for body composition is discussed online but is outside its approved purpose.

Reported adverse reactions include headache, abdominal pain, nausea, abdominal distension and dizziness. The label warns about fractures, liver test abnormalities and biliary obstruction. It is available by prescription only.

angle.text: Seladelpar is an approved PPAR-delta agonist that fat-loss circles watch because PPAR-delta activation is linked to greater fat burning and a leaner body. Its approved studies concern liver disease, not body composition.

lead: Seladelpar (brand name Livdelzi; research codes MBX-8025 and RWJ-800025) is an oral, selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPAR-delta) agonist. The US FDA approved it in August 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), together with ursodeoxycholic acid in adults with an inadequate response to it, or alone in those who cannot tolerate it.[1][2]

The approval was accelerated, based on reduction of alkaline phosphatase; the label states that improved survival or prevention of liver decompensation has not been demonstrated.[2] The drug is discussed in fat-loss and PPAR-delta contexts because it shares a target with research compounds such as GW501516, but its studied use is in liver disease, and no studies of appearance or body-composition outcomes were found.

paras: The only approved indication is primary biliary cholangitis, an autoimmune cholestatic liver disease for which options beyond ursodeoxycholic acid have been limited.[2][3][4] The EU granted conditional marketing authorization in February 2025.[1]

The US label lists headache, abdominal pain, nausea, abdominal distension and dizziness as the most common adverse reactions. Warnings cover fractures, liver test abnormalities and biliary obstruction. Human pregnancy data are insufficient to assess risk.[2]

Seladelpar activates PPAR-delta. The label says its therapeutic mechanism in PBC is not well understood; relevant activity includes reduced bile acid synthesis, which published work links to fibroblast growth factor 21 signalling and lowered CYP7A1 expression in hepatocytes.[2][5] A structural study compared how seladelpar, elafibranor and lanifibranor bind PPAR subtypes.[6]

Wikipedia reports that the compound was licensed from Janssen and developed by Metabolex under the code MBX-8025, later associated with CymaBay and Gilead.[1] Studies in diabetic obese mice reported that it reversed features of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.[7] A phase 2 trial in NASH was terminated.[8]

A 12-month phase 3 placebo-controlled trial (RESPONSE) in PBC patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA reported in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2024.[3][9] The earlier phase 3 ENHANCE trial evaluated 5 mg and 10 mg doses against placebo over three months.[10] A phase 2 proof-of-concept study in the Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology found anticholestatic effects.[11] Secondary analyses reported reductions in pruritus and interleukin-31.[12] Registered trials include one in PBC with compensated cirrhosis and a terminated NASH study.[8][13]
No studies found of seladelpar for cosmetic, fat-loss or muscle-related goals.

timeline.event: Phase 2 proof-of-concept trial in PBC published.[11]
RESPONSE phase 3 results in NEJM; FDA accelerated approval in August.[1][3]
